A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SISPDE research work. Their complete main texts and appendices A–D, including equations, proofs, tables and figures, support reliable comparison and matching of relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original OOD-detection experiments, kernel-smoothness analysis, graph-rewiring experiments and runtime measurements in Sections 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and additionally reports GEBM comparisons and an SISPDE-RBF kernel ablation in Table 1.

M1.justification: The proposed Φ-Wiener construction, Matérn-driven graph ODE, training loss and Chebyshev approximation remain unchanged. SISPDE-RBF is introduced as an experimental comparison variant; the proposed SISPDE procedure is retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight datasets under label leave-out, structural perturbation and feature perturbation. The synthetic illustration and graph-rewiring scenarios are also retained. Additional comparator results do not expand dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds reported comparisons against GEBM and SISPDE-RBF. GOLD's unchanged results already appear in v1 Table 4 and move into v2 Table 1. Although v1 Appendix C.8 names GEBM and latent graph SDE, its table contains no result rows for either; latent graph SDE therefore is not an established removed comparator.

E3.justification: The RBF experiment introduces a smooth-kernel control, described as the ν→∞ limit. Existing label assignments, perturbation procedures, metrics and hyperparameter-search ranges remain unchanged. The expanded explanation of training without OOD exposure clarifies the stated setup rather than establishing a revised training protocol.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 and Table 1 add a focused Matérn-versus-RBF ablation testing the importance of adjustable kernel smoothness, particularly on low-LI graphs. The existing best-ν analysis, rewiring experiment and runtime analysis remain. Appendix B.3 adds discussion rather than a new empirical variance study.

E5.justification: Both versions report Table 1 results as mean ± standard deviation over five runs with different seeds. The added rows follow this existing practice; no changed run count, confidence interval or significance-testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds complete GEBM and SISPDE-RBF result sets across all datasets and shifts, substantially extending the comparative evidence and changing rankings. For example, newly reported GEBM achieves 94.20 ± 4.52 Citeseer label-shift AUC versus SISPDE's retained 85.43 ± 0.80. Every existing result row, including GOLD, is numerically unchanged, as are the rewiring results.

T1.justification: New Appendix B.3 gives the spectral node-variance expression in Equation 16 and a conditional argument about variance suppression when 2ν/κ² is fixed at one. The four existing theorems and their appendix proofs are unchanged. The added main-text proof sketch for Theorem 1 summarizes reasoning already present in v1.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about structure-informed stochastic message passing, controllable covariance smoothness, theoretical guarantees and OOD-detection effectiveness across label-informativeness regimes. New comparisons support or qualify existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendix B.3 newly discusses how node variance depends on graph topology and integration time, including the unresolved interaction between noise accumulation and oversmoothing. Section 4.2 interprets the RBF results as additional support for adjustable smoothness on low-LI graphs. Existing rewiring and scalability interpretations remain.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 newly states the O(m|E|) computational cost of the existing Chebyshev approximation. Hardware, software versions, label assignments and hyperparameter-search grids in Appendix C are unchanged; no new code-access information or detailed configurations for the added comparators are supplied.

R1.justification: The same 56 references and substantive related-work discussion are retained. GOLD and GEBM were already cited in v1. Bringing them into the main comparison does not introduce new cited research or change the paper's positioning relative to GNSD, graph Gaussian processes and PDE-based message passing.

P1.justification: Localized additions clarify the spectral matrix function, summarize Theorem 1's proof, explain OOD exposure and discuss node variance. Appendix C.8 disappears after comparison results are consolidated, and the publication footer changes. Most prose and the overall section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 consolidates v1 Tables 1 and 4 into an expanded Table 1, stacks Figure 2's panels vertically, and redraws the ranking plots in Figures 2(a) and 3 with additional competitors. Other displays retain their content, including Figure 4's runtime analysis, with pagination and placement changes.

improvement.justification: The new GEBM comparison and RBF ablation make the empirical assessment more informative, while Appendix B.3 adds useful discussion of node variance. These are limited gains: v2 retains v1's unsupported 71/72 best-or-runner-up summary and does not reconcile table highlighting with new winners, such as GEBM on Citeseer label shift. The added evidence improves the paper, but its integration and interpretation remain incomplete.
